title: Leaving Willis Young for the DeParis show
summary: Money got bad with Young, who gave them only eating money; Phillips, Pete Jones and James Clark left for Sidney DeParis Sr.'s show in Baltimore.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Flemington, that's where everybody was getting ready to leave. That's when I left Mr. Young; I was getting ready to leave him.
Yeah. We went to Mobile, and stayed in Mobile. Sidney DeParis' father, we went on his show...
He had a band, too -- a show of his, right?
Yeah, he had the same kind of show Old Man Young had.
But Wilbur and Sidney, Jr. were not in the band at that time, right?
No, they wasn't with him. Wilbur had his own band in Philadelphia.
Before you get into that, could you tell just a little bit about the minstrel show? You've already mentioned the carnival...

Well, I'm still on the minstrel show. When we got down there, David... Not Goliath, but David. David had been on DeParis' show, then he told us, "Man, let's leave here..." -- because we wasn't gettin' no money with Mr. Young. He wasn't givin' us nothin' much, you know what I mean? Business got bad. He'd give us maybe 50 cents or a dollar, something like that...

I mean, to eat on. Just some eating money, we got that to live on. We got tired of that, so Mr. DeParis sent us some tickets to come to his show. That was in Mobile, Alabama. So we left Mobile, Alabama, and came to Baltimore.

I'm gonna tell you. I left. Pete Jones left. And James Clark. Three of us. Just three of us left. We went to Baltimore. This show opened up in Baltimore. It was called (?)Bernard (?) Show. It was the same like Billy Clark's show. All of them... At that time there was a lot of carnivals out like that, that had shows on. They called them a jig show.
